newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state to sell at least 10 pct of miller.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state to sell at least 10 pct of miller.

text.p: The Egyptian state said on Sunday it was offering the public at least 400,000 shares, or 10 percent, of Alexandria Flour Mills and fixed the initial offer price at 75 pounds ($22.10) a share.

The state-owned Holding Company for Rice and Flour Mills said in a published announcement it could increase the stake on offer to a maximum 30 percent of the firm's total four million shares. The state will also sell the employee shareholder association of Alexandria Flour Mills another 10 percent.

The offer comes as part of the state's privatisation-led economic reform programme. The state has previously sold part of its stake in several milling firms but it has said it will not relinquish its majority control of the sector because of its "strategic nature".

The offer opens on June 29 for two days and the sale will be carried out according to the discovery price system, where the final selling price can be lower or higher than the initial 75 pounds, the company added.

Individuals can apply for a minimum of 25 shares. The announcement did not spell out the minimum number of shares that institutions can buy. Milling shares are among the most popular stocks traded on the Cairo stock exchange.
Shareholders will get the forecast dividend of at least 5.00 pounds at least for the fiscal year 1996/97 which ends on June 30. The firm gave a 1.7 pound dividend for the previous year.
The state National Bank of Egypt (NBE) and the Commercial International Investment Company (CIIC) are agents for the sale.
